items: Battles now open and close like the handhelds: the screen flashes and wipes into battle, wild Pokémon slide in under a "A wild … appeared!" box, trainers get a versus screen and send their Pokémon out of balls, a sweeping banner marks each new round, a chip and a red board edge show the foe's turn, and the results card fills each Pokémon's EXP bar (with level-ups), lists the spoils and presents a won badge.

Battle feel: hits blink the Pokémon and knock it back after a beat of hit-stop, "It's super effective!" pops up with a shake, damage numbers stack instead of overlapping, fainted Pokémon sink into the ground, Poké Balls fly, draw the Pokémon in, wobble and click (or burst open), and statuses show as BRN/PAR/PSN/SLP/FRZ pills with Zzz, sparks, embers or circling stars.

Battle fixes: Pokémon stand on their shadows (flyers hover and bob), a gold arrow marks whose turn it is, HP bars drain with a trailing segment (red under 20%), the walk area is a light outline that clears when it should, range rings stay on the board, trainer and Gym battles use their own arena look, flames no longer burn on rocks, clearer log wording.

Battlefields reworked to look like a Pokémon route: rocks, cover and water never pile on each other any more; cover is tall grass (moss in caves, dune grass on the shore); brighter grass and warmer sand; Pokémon stand on a flat shadow with a thin team ring and a framed HP bar; the Full log button fits its label.
Cave battlefields have loose stones lying about again.

The battle ground is back to its hand-drawn look (shaded rocks, leafy bushes, grass with flowers); the effects stay on top of it: rippling water, real flames, bubbling poison and light from fire and attacks.

Faster battles, kinder to phones: the still part of the battle ground is worked out once instead of every frame, the moving part (water, flames, light) runs at half resolution and 30 fps, and hovering a foe no longer recalculates its reach on every mouse move.
Camp: the top buttons are as wide as their labels, so Feedback is no longer bigger than the rest.
The walkable area has a smooth, rounded edge instead of steps; rocks are drawn exactly where they block (no more merged boulders over open ground); loose pebbles lie about, most of them in caves.
Helping Hand explained clearly: the ally gets +25% damage on its next turn, and the user gets it too (it is no longer listed as a "price").
Burning ground is now real flames painted on the ground (no more dots), poisoned ground a bubbling sludge, and mud no longer has flickering light squares.

The battle ground is now painted per pixel on the graphics card, from code: grass with tufts and flowers, boulders with real relief and shadows, leafy bush canopies, water with moving ripples, caustics and foam, wet mud. Burning ground and attacks light up the ground around them.

Battlefield terrain redrawn: rocks with shadows, a lit top face and creases; bushes as round leafy canopies; water deepening towards the middle with a foamy shore; wet mud with glossy spots; the ground is no longer a checkerboard.

Living battlefields: burning ground flickers and smokes, poison bubbles, mud pops; area attacks land with a shockwave, dust and a shake; hits leave scorches, cracks, wet splashes, frost and leaves on the ground for the rest of the battle; ground turning into water, mud, grass or rock bursts out; drifting motes, glinting water, shaded edges and shadows under every Pokémon.

No more 5-round cooldowns: Fell Stinger, Cross Poison, Rock Blast, Fake Out and most self-buffs now 3; Dark Pulse, Power Gem, Razor Wind, Silver Wind, Stomping Tantrum 2; Belly Drum, Dragon Dance, Substitute 4.

Equipment tab: held items in the bag are a compact 3-column grid you can scroll (wheel or arrows); tap one to equip it. Potions, Rare Candy and remedies share one row, Take off sits beside the held item.

Evolution is a big moment now: its own scene after the battle (or after a Rare Candy), the silhouette flickering between the two forms, a flash, the new form. Stop it once and it waits: start it any time with the Evolve button on its Pokémon screen.
Evolution levels raised so every first form can be caught in the wild where it lives (e.g. Zubat 15, Geodude 16, Magikarp 22); the wild Pokémon list shows which form appears at which level.
Map: the wild group preview names the form you will actually fight (a Lv 10 Zubat already shows as Golbat).
Battle: "Enemy turn…" no longer shows while your own Pokémon is attacking or moving.
Items have icons too, in the bag, the shop and on the Pokémon screen's Equipment tab (potions, berries, Rare Candy, every held item and key item).
Shop: the scroll arrows no longer cover the Buy buttons, and the list no longer runs under the hint at the bottom.
Ball icons look like the real ones (the Ultra Ball has its yellow bands, the Great Ball its red patches) and are the same everywhere: map, bag, shop, battle.
Brock is gentler: his Onix is Lv 9 (was 11), the gym trainer and Viridian Forest are closer in level, so the first gym is no wall.
Map: the party sits in a 3×3 grid, the money and items in a column beside it, the balls as their icons with the count.

UI polish: a party of 7–9 shows in two rows on the map; the Moves tab marks basic ◆, special ■ and Bond ▲ (filled: in use); the Stats tab explains a stat at all times and the header no longer repeats the stats; the bag no longer says 0× for worn items; the starter cards and meal texts read better.
Camp: the party in a 3×3 grid, storage on the right in two columns (up to 17 shown).
Deployment: compact party cards (name beside the portrait, level and knockouts on the card).
The party holds 9 Pokémon (was 10), so every one fits the deployment cards; a 10th from an old save waits in storage.
A foe's info shows its level; the raw stats are gone from it.
A new round slides in over the battlefield ("Round 2"), so it is clear why a Pokémon acts again.
Pokémon screen: To storage / To party sits in the header by the pager, on every tab.
Balls fly up to 4 away (was 3).
Moves that burst around the user (Earthquake…) say so: ◎2 in the move lists, "around itself" in the details, instead of range 0.
Trainers on the map are people now, dressed by class (Youngster cap, Bug Catcher net, Hiker backpack, Rocket black…), their lead Pokémon small at their side.
Bigger battles wait for badges: 3 Pokémon a side until your first badge, one more slot per badge up to the map's size.
Burn no longer lowers damage dealt, only hurts each turn; Fairy moves now Soften (−15% damage) instead of Weaken.

Moves that were copies now follow their canon twists: Charm, Feather Dance and Eerie Impulse weaken longer; Sand Attack, Kinesis and Flash blind; Baby-Doll Eyes is quicker; Strength Sap heals the user; Memento weakens and exposes at a cost of HP; Thunder Wave has no effect on Ground types (Glare does).
Smokescreen now blinds: the target's ranged moves reach 1 less for 2 turns (Confide still weakens).
The turn passes on its own again when only a sliver of movement is left and no move has anything in reach.
Wild Pokémon here works on paths too: it lists the nearest grass or cave of the map.
The bag lists your key items (Old Amber and the like) with what they are for.
Each portrait in the turn order shows its Pokémon's level.

Move lists (battle and Pokémon screen) are grouped by kind, a thin line between basic attacks, skills and Bond moves; the battle panel drops its repeated headers; a Bond move shows its cost as Bond pips (●●) on its button; icons instead of words: ⚔ power, ⏳ cooldown, ✕ no target, ↔ reach, 👣 movement, and the balls themselves on the ball buttons.

Mastery trees rebuilt: every row offers one kind of move. Lv 3 and Lv 24 Bond moves, Lv 6 and Lv 12 a skill plus a utility (Disable, Helping Hand, Knock Off…), Lv 18 a second basic attack to swap in for coverage.
A move's kind is now its own: big hits (canon power 85+) are Bond moves, weak plain hits are basic attacks, everything else is a skill.
Momentum (the Speed bonus after moving) no longer counts against the foe you began the turn engaged with: stepping out and back in gains nothing.
New utility moves: Follow Me, Helping Hand, Ally Switch and Knock Off (coming to the mastery trees).
Mastery trees only offer passives that help the line's role: a melee line gets Pin Down or Tough Claws where a ranged one gets Far Sight or Long Reach.
After a trainer battle the money is shown once, as one total (the prize was listed separately).
Battle maps: a rock wall always leaves room for three Pokémon abreast to pass (some had a gap only one wide).
Wild Pokémon no longer step out of an engagement just to step back in; a melee one leaves only when it is worth it.
On phones the game can be installed: Add to Home screen opens it fullscreen like an app (always the latest version).
Big moves have a price: Double-Edge and Head Smash hurt the user too, Superpower weakens it, Outrage confuses it; they hit a little harder for it.

New move effects: Double Hit lands twice, Chip Away and Feint Attack ignore protective buffs, False Swipe never knocks out (handy for catching), Lash Out hits harder while the user has an ailment, Mach Punch dashes in.
Guillotine now finishes off hurt foes instead of simply out-hitting everything.
Every Lv 3 focus is a real choice: no option is just a stronger copy of another.
The music is a little quieter.
A ball icon on the browser tab, and a picture when the link is shared.
Tab icon, and on phones the game can be installed: Add to Home screen opens it fullscreen like an app.
Fixed: Oddish and 38 other Pokémon started without a skill (their starting move had turned into a Bond move).
Super Fang takes half the target's current HP; Endeavor, Flail and Reversal hit harder the more HP the user has lost; Brine hits hurt targets harder, Wring Out healthy ones.
Seel and Dewgong start with Icy Wind, Horsea and Seadra with Twister, Omanyte and Omastar with Rock Throw.
Pokémon screen: portrait on the left, navigation top right, like the Camp.
Music: chiptune loops by Juhani Junkala on the title, the map and in battle.
Map legend tip on the first map visit and a ? help on the map.
A turn with nothing left to do passes on its own; End turn also drops a selected ball.
One-time tips the first time something comes up (engagement, catching, knockouts, focus, camp…), and a ? help listing them.
A wild group you avoided or fled from leaves you alone for a few steps.
The title screen replays recorded battles behind the menu.
Feedback form on the title, in camp and after battles.
Pokédex: every species you met, with stats, role, ability, evolutions, starting moves and its whole mastery tree.
